content:
Electrical-network insurance assessment starts with whose equipment is involved and what has happened. A company's transformer, an operator's line and a customer's machinery are different assets. Electricity can stop without physical damage to company property, so an outage alone does not establish an insured loss.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. Planning material for 2027; the scenarios below are hypothetical, not incident or demand forecasts.

Who should organize the review?

Manufacturers, warehouses, agricultural businesses and other companies dependent on electrical installations should identify the equipment they own or use. Record the relevant lease, connection and service relationships. A site's name does not explain ownership of every component supporting it.

Prepare a descriptive inventory with documented values and the actual operating stage. Separate new installation or testing from equipment already in use. Avoid sharing operational access details or security-sensitive plans through public forms.

Which events and exclusions matter?

Ask about fire, accidental physical damage and internal breakdown as distinct issues. Request the proposed treatment of electrical causes based on the actual technical findings; the article does not diagnose a fault from a photograph or an outage report.

Clarify wear, known defects, planned replacement, inadequate maintenance and losses caused only by external supply interruption. These questions do not establish universal exclusions. Where additional interruption protection is proposed, check the required triggering event, affected activity, limits and applicable periods.

What could change for the business in 2027?

An added production line, charging installation or battery system can change the equipment inventory and the consequences of a stoppage. A BESS configuration review can help describe added storage separately from the supply network. This is a reason to reassess changed operations, not a prediction that demand or outages will rise. Technical specialists must evaluate the actual connection, capacity and protective arrangements.

Use a hypothetical exercise: production stops, but the initial observation does not establish whether the cause lies inside or outside the site. Retain competent findings and operator communications separately from assumptions. Do not name a preferred cause simply because it appears easier to insure.

Prevention before an incident

Arrange competent review of maintenance records, unresolved recommendations and the realistic availability of compatible spare parts. Identify the person receiving warnings and the authorized service contact. The presence of a spare component in a catalogue does not prove immediate availability or safe compatibility.

Check recovery dependencies with operational staff: diagnosis, procurement, fitting and testing after repair. Do not change protective equipment or perform measurements based on an insurance article. Safety and authorized technical procedures remain separate from document collection.

How is the price assessed?

There is no verified fixed premium for your 2027 installation here. A calculation requires equipment, values, locations, condition, activity, history and the risks and limits requested. The premium is the amount paid for insurance. A deductible is the share of a loss retained by the insured under the contract. (BNM: contract terms, checked 25 November 2026; general guidance, not individual policy conditions.)

Compare identical equipment lists and periods. Ask whether inspection, access, transport, installation and emergency expenses are included or limited. Prepare production effects separately: a damaged transformer's value does not quantify every business consequence, and all stopped sales cannot simply be called lost profit.

Documents for an initial discussion

Organize inventory and ownership records, purchase or replacement evidence, commissioning documents, maintenance history and known issues. Add a high-level description of affected business activities if interruption is being considered. Technical drawings should follow only through an agreed channel when needed.

Three situations: what to compare before deciding

The MOLDASIG property page, rechecked on 26 November 2026, distinguishes machinery-breakdown and interruption categories. It does not verify dedicated operating-network wording or automatic protection for external outages.

  • Company transformer fails: compare ownership and the named equipment with competent findings and maintenance. Prepare the asset list and values. Check definitions for the cause and component rather than assuming every electrical fault is accepted.
  • External supply stops but equipment is intact: compare operator communications and actual consequences. Prepare the service agreement and safely available timing. Ask separately about external interruption and required trigger; an outage report is not confirmation.
  • Solar, charging or storage equipment is added in 2027: compare the new configuration and dependencies with the old schedule. Prepare commissioning and value records. Keep technical acceptance and the insurer’s response separate before relying on unchanged insurance.

Frequently asked questions

What factors determine the installation premium?

Identify the equipment, owner, supported values, locations, technical condition, activity, history and requested risks. Compare the same period, deductible and expense limits. A transformer supporting one process and an installation supplying several critical activities may need different descriptions; neither equipment power nor purchase price alone establishes a verified premium.

What records should a company prepare?

Organize the inventory, ownership or use documents, purchase or replacement evidence, commissioning records, maintenance history and known issues. Describe business dependencies at a high level. Detailed drawings and sensitive operational information should follow only through an agreed channel when needed; the enquiry should not require public system access.

What should we do after a power interruption or suspected fault?

Follow competent electrical and safety instructions, not an online article. Record safely available timing, operator communications and authorized findings. Keep an external outage separate from evidence of internal damage. Notify according to the actual policy and request inspection instructions; do not perform measurements or restart unsafe equipment to establish a claim.

Does company property insurance pay for every external outage?

No automatic conclusion follows from a property-policy title. Ask whether physical damage is required and how external supply interruption and resulting financial loss are treated. Read the accepted event, limits and periods. A repair bill, production stoppage or operator notice does not independently establish payment for all consequences.

What changes when we add a production line, charger or battery?

Update the inventory and explain the new dependencies before assuming that the existing programme is unchanged. Competent specialists assess the technical connection and safety; the insurer considers the declared risk and conditions. Keep technical acceptance, internal investment approval and the insurance reply as distinct documents with their actual dates.

Discuss the installation with ING Broker. The broker does not certify electrical safety or guarantee acceptance. Availability, exclusions, risk acceptance and compensation depend on the insurer's actual contract.
